item.title: Paper: Army Must Transform for Rapid, Unforgiving Fight
item.description: To succeed in large-scale combat operations, the Army must adapt to a future fight that is rapid, unforgiving and offers no sanctuary, according to a new paper published by the Association of the U.S. Army.

item.title: National Guard Activates Special Purpose Brigade
item.description: The District of Columbia National Guard has activated the 260th Special Purpose Brigade, the only brigade in the Army specifically designed to coordinate military support to civil authorities and protect critical infrastructure in the nation’s capital.

item.title: Army Veteran, Teammates Win Para Ice Hockey Gold
item.description: Team USA clinched the gold medal in para ice hockey after dominating Canada in the final at the 2026 Winter Paralympics in Milan and Cortina, Italy. “No description needed,” Team USA’s goalie and Army veteran Jen Lee wrote on Instagram with a montage of photos of the team celebrating their 6-2 win to a remix of Lynyrd Skynyrd’s Free Bird.

item.title: Obadal: Army Building Modern, Dominant Land Force
item.description: From the Army’s organic industrial base to its installations, the service is working to provide soldiers with the capabilities they need to fight on a complex future battlefield, Army Undersecretary Michael Obadal said. Speaking March 24 during a keynote address to open the Association of the U.S. Army’s 2026 Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama, Obadal called on industry to work with the Army as it seeks dominance on the battlefield.

item.title: Army Restructures for Acquisition Speed
item.description: The Army’s six newly created portfolio acquisition executives are a cornerstone of the service’s transformation efforts, leaders said. Appearing together for the first time, representatives from all six portfolio acquisition executives, or PAEs, spoke on a panel March 24 during the Association of the U.S. Army’s Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama.

item.title: Civilian Workforce Vital to Army Transformation
item.description: Army civilians are integral to building soldier lethality and are helping to drive the service’s transformation, a panel of senior Army leaders said. In remarks during a panel discussion March 24 at the Association of the U.S. Army’s Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama, Bill Moore, a retired War Department senior executive, noted that “it’s been kind of a tough year for Army civilians” as the federal government has pared down the size of the workforce.

item.title: Army Launches Unmanned Aircraft Systems Marketplace
item.description: Continuing its push to transform, the Army has launched the Unmanned Aircraft Systems Marketplace, a new digital storefront designed to get trusted, cutting-edge drone technology into the hands of soldiers. Announced on March 24 during the Association of the U.S. Army’s Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama, the digital one-stop shop will allow Army units, government partners and allied nations to efficiently procure vetted UAS solutions, the service said in a news release

item.title: Mohan: Army, Industry Partnerships More Important Than Ever
item.description: In the past year, the Army has leveraged its relationships with industry as it pushes to “keep up and keep pace” with fast moving technology and ever-growing threats, the commanding general of U.S. Army Materiel Command said. “We are in a time of continuous transformation in the Army, … and the pace continues,” Lt. Gen. Chris Mohan said in keynote remarks March 25 at the Association of the U.S. Army’s Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama.

item.title: Combat Training Centers Transform to Further Test Units
item.description: With the establishment of U.S. Army Transformation and Training Command, the Army’s combat training centers are back under the control of U.S. Army Combined Arms Command, and big changes are coming, a senior Army leader said. Lt. Gen. James Isenhower, commanding general of Combined Arms Command at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, said the shift is beneficial because it aligns proponency, funding and resource allocation for the combat training centers, known as CTCs, under a singular headquarters.

item.title: Army’s New Campus-Style Dining Venues Take Off
item.description: Soldiers are so satisfied with the Army’s new food options that the service is moving as fast as possible to replicate it on more installations, senior Army sustainment officials said. “We’ve come light years” from the days where dining facility food was Salisbury steak and coffee from a mermite container that tasted like the vegetable soup that was in it the night before, said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, commanding general of the U.S. Army Sustainment Command.

item.title: Young Leaders Network, Learn at Gen Next Forum
item.description: Lessons in leadership, resilience and career progression were part of the discussion for some 50 young professionals who attended the Generation Next Forum at the Association of the U.S. Army’s Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama. item.description: The mission of U.S. Army Transformation and Training Command is to enable the Army to defeat all adversaries by adapting to the ever-changing character of war, its commanding general said. item.description: The old rules of warfare are gone, and the Army is preparing for a future battlefield that’s swarming with drones, a panel of leaders said during a Warriors Corner presentation at the Association of the U.S. Army’s 2026 Global Force Symposium and Exposition in Huntsville, Alabama. “The battlefield has a new predator,” said Col. item.title: Tricare Options Available for Displaced Beneficiaries
item.description: Tricare beneficiaries who were displaced from an overseas duty station or their home abroad back to the U.S. are still covered by Tricare, according to the Tricare website. “If you were recently displaced from an overseas duty station or your home abroad, you’re still covered by Tricare,” according to a Tricare handout for displaced beneficiaries. “This displacement counts as a qualifying life event, which opens a 90-day window for you to update your Tricare region or make enrollment changes.”

item.title: AUSA Hosts 9th Annual Operation Deploy Your Dress Event
item.description: The Association of the U.S. Army and Operation Deploy Your Dress are teaming up again this year for a free pop-up event featuring more than 3,000 cocktail dresses and formal gowns. Volunteers from the two organizations will welcome military or dependent ID card holders of all ranks and services for the ninth annual Operation Deploy Your Dress D.C. This year’s event will take place April 25 at AUSA headquarters in Arlington, Virginia.
